name: Christensen transanal irrigation
question: In adults with spinal cord injury and neurogenic bowel dysfunction, does transanal irrigation improve bowel symptoms compared with conservative bowel management?

design.blinding: No blinding; the interventions made blinding impossible
design.population: Adults with spinal cord injury and neurogenic bowel dysfunction treated at five specialized European spinal cord injury centers.
design.locator: Full text, Patients and Methods, pp 738–741; Table 1

verdictNote: Constipation and fecal incontinence scores favored irrigation at 10 weeks.
takeaway: In 87 adults with spinal cord injury and neurogenic bowel dysfunction, transanal irrigation improved constipation and fecal incontinence scores versus conservative bowel management after 10 weeks.

reports.label: Randomized comparison
reports.dateLocator: PubMed citation, September 2006 issue; exact day not stated
reports.citation: Christensen P, Bazzocchi G, Coggrave M, et al. "A Randomized, Controlled Trial of Transanal Irrigation Versus Conservative Bowel Management in Spinal Cord–Injured Patients." *Gastroenterology.* 2006;131(3):738-747. doi:10.1053/j.gastro.2006.06.004
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Abstract and Assessments During the Study, pp 738–740

results.measure: Mean Cleveland Clinic constipation score at 10 weeks (0–30; lower is better)
results.note: Intention-to-treat analysis included 39 irrigation and 41 conservative-care participants; missing termination assessments used baseline observations carried forward.
results.locator: Full text, Table 3; Statistical Analysis, p 741

results.measure: Mean St. Mark's fecal incontinence score at 10 weeks (0–24; lower is better)
results.note: Intention-to-treat analysis included 42 irrigation and 45 conservative-care participants, with baseline observations carried forward for missing termination assessments.

results.measure: Mean Neurogenic Bowel Dysfunction score at 10 weeks (0–47; lower is better)
results.note: Intention-to-treat analysis included 41 irrigation and 45 conservative-care participants; missing termination assessments used baseline observations carried forward.

results.measure: Mean improvement in quality of life at 10 weeks on a 0–10 numeric box scale (higher is better)
results.note: Only assessed at termination; the score was not recorded at baseline.
results.locator: Full text, Table 3; Assessments During the Study, p 740

results.measure: Mean minutes spent on bowel management daily during weeks 7–10
results.note: Steady-state weekly follow-up; last observation carried forward.

harms.label: Urinary tract infection treated with antibiotics
harms.note: P = 0.0052; the paper gives percentages without event counts or arm-specific assessed denominators.

harms.label: Hospitalization for severe abdominal pain

values.exp: 2/42 randomized patients after 3 and 9 weeks of treatment

harms.note: No serious condition was found; both improved after disimpaction. One discontinued treatment.

delivery.label: Irrigation water volume and frequency
delivery.value: Peristeen balloon catheter and manual pump; usual starting regimen 750 mL tepid tap water daily, adjustable to 250–1500 mL and every second day or less. During weeks 7–10, median volume was 700 mL (range 200–1500) among 37 users; 6 irrigated daily, 18 every second day, and 13 one to three times weekly.

reports.label: Pooled irrigation cohort and predictors
reports.citation: Christensen P, Bazzocchi G, Coggrave M, et al. "Outcome of Transanal Irrigation for Bowel Dysfunction in Patients With Spinal Cord Injury." *J Spinal Cord Med.* 2008;31(5):560-567. doi:10.1080/10790268.2008.11754571
reports.followUp: 10 weeks of irrigation; includes 20 patients crossing over after conservative management

results.measure: Mean within-group change in Cleveland Clinic constipation score after 10 weeks of irrigation
results.note: Pooled 62-patient irrigation cohort; not a second randomized comparison.

results.measure: Mean within-group change in St. Mark's fecal incontinence score after 10 weeks of irrigation
results.note: Pooled 62-patient irrigation cohort; not a second randomized comparison.

results.measure: Mean within-group change in Neurogenic Bowel Dysfunction score after 10 weeks of irrigation
results.note: Pooled 62-patient irrigation cohort; not a second randomized comparison.

harms.label: Device problems leading to withdrawal

values.exp: 5 catheter expulsions; 1 water leak; 1 balloon burst

harms.note: Among 62 patients offered irrigation, four withdrew during training because of repeated catheter expulsion, one for leakage, one later for expulsion, and one for balloon burst. One additional patient withdrew because of an unspecified adverse event.

delivery.label: Irrigation procedure and training
delivery.value: Peristeen coated rectal balloon catheter, manual pump and water container; lukewarm tap water instilled after balloon inflation, then catheter removal and evacuation; specialist-nurse training.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods, Transanal Irrigation; Figure 1

delivery.label: Irrigation discontinuation
delivery.value: 17/62 (27.4%) stopped during the 10-week irrigation period; 7/17 had no termination assessment.
